page: Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. This configuration delivers 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% of tested instances via stress-ng. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is also strong, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25%, while large-block memory bandwidth read and write speeds remain in the middle 50% average tier. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 342.31 tokens per second using a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for the same model and overall performance on medium 7B models align with average tier results. Database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations all perform within the middle 50% benchmark range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio offer a predictable resource allocation without the performance degradation risks associated with shared-core environments. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides a reliable storage-to-compute balance for data-intensive tasks. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded applications, general-purpose web serving, database hosting, and moderate-scale language model inference tasks.
